fields.h1: Build Bookkeeping Automation Around the Ledger You Use
fields.hero_description: Build bookkeeping automation that files each receipt with its charge and codes bank lines in the accounting software you run.
fields.features_heading: The Bookkeeping Week, Run by Rules
fields.features_subheading: Bookkeeping automation codes each transaction by rule and leaves the exceptions to a person. Emergent builds it from a prompt.
fields.feature_1:
Posts to the ledger you already keep

Connects to QuickBooks or Xero, or any other accounting software with an API. Coded lines sync into the ledger, and the chart of accounts syncs back for every rule to pick from.
fields.feature_2:
Receipts become fields, not attachments

Reads a receipt photo or an emailed PDF into merchant, date, total, and tax. A blurry or torn total goes to a person to confirm instead of being guessed into the books.
fields.feature_3:
Every coding choice keeps its history

Stores each transaction with its receipt and the rule or person that coded it, in a database you own. When a March number looks wrong, you see who picked the account and when.
fields.feature_4:
One dashboard of what is still open

Builds a dashboard of every uncoded bank line and missing receipt for the month. The bookkeeper starts each morning from that list instead of scrolling the full bank feed.
fields.feature_5:
No task cap at month-end

Runs every match and every reminder at month-end with no task cap, whether the bank feed holds 300 lines or 30,000. A busy month never stops halfway through the books.
fields.feature_6:
The code sits in your GitHub

Exports the app, its rules, and its database schema to your GitHub repository on paid plans. Your accountant or developer can read exactly how a payee rule picks an account.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Jobs That Fill a Bookkeeper's Week
fields.tab_content_1:
An $86.40 receipt finds its card charge

Kiri Vanterpool photographs an $86.40 receipt from Dockside Supply for packing tape and labels. The app reads the merchant, date, and total and attaches the photo to the $86.40 charge on her company card. A charge with no receipt after 3 days sends her a reminder.
fields.tab_content_2:
After one pick, Rook Valley Signs has a rule

A $212.00 charge from Rook Valley Signs arrives in March with no payee rule. It waits for Bettina Ruark, the bookkeeper, who codes it to Advertising. The app saves her pick as the rule for that payee, and in April the next $212.00 charge is coded on arrival and synced to the ledger.
fields.tab_content_3:
Missing statements turn into tasks on the 8th

Kestrelpoint Bookkeeping keeps the books for 38 clients. On the 2nd, each client gets an email with an upload link for last month's bank and card statements. Anyone who has not uploaded by the 5th gets a reminder. On the 8th, Thornmere Florist's missing card statement becomes a task for Amos Reyburn.
fields.tab_content_4:
Four unknown charges, one list on Friday

Every Friday, owner Leo Castellane gets the bank lines that match no payee rule and no receipt, one question per screen on his phone. There are 4 this week, starting with $412.00 to Seabright Packaging. He taps Shipping supplies, and the app codes the line and saves his answer for Bettina to review.

fields.howto_description: Seven steps to set up bookkeeping automation on the ledger you use, one job at a time, tested on last month's bank feed first.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Pick one job and write its rule
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Connect the ledger and the bank feed
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write down the bookkeeping work that comes back every week or month: chasing receipts, coding bank lines, requesting statements, and asking the owner about unknown charges. Next to each job, note who does it today and how many hours it takes.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Choose the job that takes the most hours and write its rule with real values. Name the bank account it reads, the payees it covers, the account each payee maps to, and how many days a missing receipt can wait before a reminder.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Connect your accounting software through its API, or start from an export of your chart of accounts and last month's transactions. Copy the account names exactly as the ledger spells them. A rule that names an account the ledger lacks has nowhere to post.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Tell Emergent what starts each run, what the app checks, and who gets the exceptions. Emergent writes the workflow and the screens your bookkeeper reviews exceptions in. To change a rule later, describe the change in a new prompt and Emergent updates the app.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Run last month's transactions through the app before it writes anything to the ledger. Compare each account it picks with the one your bookkeeper chose, line by line, and fix the rule wherever the two disagree. Look hardest at payees that appear only once.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Keep a person on new payees
fields.howto_step_6_des: For the first month, have the bookkeeper approve every line the app codes before it syncs. Once a full month of approvals agrees with the rules, let coded lines sync straight to the ledger and keep the review queue for new payees only.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Build the second job on the same tables. Statement requests reuse the client list you already set up, and the owner's Friday questions read the same uncoded lines the bookkeeper sees. Each new job starts from records you have already cleaned up.

faq_plan.a: Bookkeeping is the recording of financial transactions. Bookkeeping automation records the repeat ones by rule: it pairs each receipt with its card charge, assigns bank lines to accounts, and asks for missing documents. A person still handles each line that no rule covers.

faq_plan.q: How do I set up bookkeeping automation?
faq_plan.a: Start with one job, such as coding bank lines by payee. Describe its trigger, its rule, and who reviews the exceptions to Emergent's AI automation builder, and it builds the workflow and connects it to your accounting software. As new payees appear, you change the rules by prompting again.

faq_plan.q: Which tasks should bookkeeping automation handle first?
faq_plan.a: Automate the tasks that repeat on a schedule and follow one rule every time: matching receipts to card charges and coding bank lines from payees you see each month. Leave year-end adjustments and one-off entries with your bookkeeper, because each one needs a judgment call.

faq_plan.q: Can bookkeeping automation read paper receipts?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Emergent builds an app that takes the merchant name and the total off a photo of a paper receipt, then keeps the photo with the transaction it matches. The same reading step handles supplier price lists and handwritten forms, which is the work of data entry automation. Ask cardholders to photograph each receipt the day they get it, before it fades or goes missing.

faq_plan.q: How does bookkeeping automation decide which account a transaction belongs to?
faq_plan.a: It uses payee rules: each payee maps to one account, set the first time your bookkeeper codes it. Add a condition where one payee covers two kinds of spend, such as an amount limit that sends any charge over $2,000 from that payee back to the bookkeeper. Review the rule list each quarter and delete payees you no longer pay.

faq_plan.q: What should a bookkeeper still review after setting up bookkeeping automation?
faq_plan.a: Review two things: lines no rule covers, and any charge above a dollar limit you set. Approve rule changes before they apply to new lines, and keep the month-end reconciliation sign-off with a person. Every coded line and its review sit in a database you own.

faq_plan.q: Can bookkeeping automation handle vendor bills too?
faq_plan.a: Yes, as a separate workflow from the bank feed. A bill arrives before it is paid: the app reads it, holds it for approval, and later matches the payment line to it. Reading bills and creating customer invoices is covered in depth under invoice automation, and the bookkeeping side picks up each payment when it clears the bank.

faq_plan.q: How does bookkeeping automation track clients who are behind on documents?
faq_plan.a: It keeps one row per client per month, with a status for each document you need, sorted by days outstanding. A client who is late two months running needs a phone call, not another email. Emergent builds the tracker and the client upload page from a prompt, on a database you own.

faq_plan.q: Does bookkeeping automation work with the accounting software I already use?
faq_plan.a: Yes. An app built with Emergent works against your current ledger through its API: it reads the chart of accounts and writes coded lines back. If your software has no API, start from a monthly export and import the coded lines yourself.

faq_plan.q: How do payroll entries fit into bookkeeping automation?
faq_plan.a: They come in as bank withdrawals to match, while the pay run stays in its own workflow. Timesheets, approvals, and the run itself belong to payroll automation. On the bookkeeping side, the app matches each payroll withdrawal to its pay run by date and amount, and any withdrawal with no matching run goes to your bookkeeper.

plan.angle: The top 10 are bookkeeping software and fintech vendors (Dext, Ramp, QuickBooks, Booke, Pilot, Mercury, TaxDome) selling their own product, plus explainers and a Reddit thread on what can be automated end to end. None shows a rule running on real numbers. This page shows the four jobs that eat a bookkeeper's week, each with its trigger, its rule and the record it writes: a receipt photo matched to its card charge, a payee coded once and then by rule, monthly statement requests a firm sends to 38 clients, and one Friday list of unknown charges for the owner. Everything runs on top of the ledger the business already uses, and none of it is tax or accounting advice.
